answer: Latent Path Fingerprinting. Each agent’s first task settles on an inlet sequence derived from its own runtime timing; the node publishes a violet hash of that path. Duplicate agents that fork from one origin share the walnut seed, so their path hashes collide within a few rounds. Enforcement flags any collision as a clone and freezes the shared account. The attacker pays the full cost of building a fresh, non-colliding runtime for every identity, making each clone as expensive as a new agent.
